और पढ़ेंबिहार के 15 जिलों में भारी वर्षा की चेतावनी जारी।राजधानी सहित सभी जिलों के मौसम में 24 घंटे के दौरान बदलाव के आसार हैं। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र पटना के अनुसार बंगाल की खाड़ी में बने गहरे दबाव के चक्रवाती तूफान में बदलने के साथ अगले 24-48 घंटे में राजधानी समेत पूरे बिहार के मौसम का मिजाज बदलने के आसार हैं। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र, पटना के अनुसार ओडिशा, बंगाल से लेकर उत्तर प्रदेश तक इसका व्यापक प्रभाव देखने को मिल सकता है। प्रदेश में अगले दो दिनों तक अलग-अलग हिस्सों में वर्षा की गतिविधियां बनी रहेंगी। प्रदेश के 15 जिलों के अलग-अलग भागों में भारी व अति भारी वर्षा को लेकर चेतावनी जारी की गई। पटना सहित सभी जिलों में मेघ गर्जन, वज्रपात और कई स्थानों पर आंधी-पानी को लेकर स्थिति बने रहने की संभावना है। कई स्थानों पर 40-50 किमी प्रतिघंटा की रफ्तार से हवा चलने की संभावना है। पूर्वी चंपारण, गोपालगंज, मुजफ्फरपुर, सिवान एवं पश्विमी चंपारण जिले में अति भारी वर्षा एवं अररिया, भभुआ, भोजपुर, बक्सर, किशनगंज, पूर्णिया, सारण, शिवहर, सीतामढ़ी एवं सुपौल में भारी वर्षा को लेकर चेतावनी जारी की गई है। प्रदेश में अगले दो दिनों अलग-अलग भागों में वर्षा की गतिविधियां बने रहने के आसार है। बीते 24 घंटे के दौरान प्रदेश के अलग-अलग भागों में वर्षा दर्ज की गई। बांका के फुल्लीडुमर में 45.2 मिमी सर्वाधिक वर्षा दर्ज की गई। बुधवार को औरंगाबाद, नालंदा एवं शेखपुरा को छोड़ कर पटना सहित शेष जिलों के अधिकतम तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई। पटना का अधिकतम तापमान तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट के साथ 33.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस 36.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस के साथ भभुआ के कैमूर में सर्वाधिक तापमान दर्ज किया गया। बुधवार को पटना सहित आसपास इलाकों में दिन भर उमस के साथ शाम में बूंदाबांदी से मौसम सामान्य बना रहा। राजधानी सहित गया, भागलपुर, डेहरी,वैशाली में बूंदाबांदी और तेज हवा से मौसम सामान्य बना रहा।मुजफ्फरपुर के सराय में 36.8 मिमी, मुंगेर के संग्रामपुर में 36.2 मिमी, किशनगंज के ठाकुरगंज में 32.4 मिमी, बांका के रजौन में 30.6 मिमी, भोजपुर के कोइलवर में 28 मिमी, खगड़िया के बालतारा में 26.4 मिमी दर्ज की गई। पटना के बिहटा में 24.2 मिमी, जमुई में 20.4 मिमी, मधेपुरा के कुमारखंड में 20.2 मिमी, जमुई के खैरा में 18.2 मिमी, Red alert for 4 Odisha districts as deep depression triggers heavy rain threat A deep depression crossing into Odisha is expected to bring heavy to very heavy rain through September 26. The IMD has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in several southern districts, with flash floods and landslides among the risks. Watch: Heavy #Rain Continues In #Odisha As #BayofBengal Depression Intensifies Odisha is bracing for another spell of heavy to very heavy rainfall as a deep depression that crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast moves inland, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning of extremely heavy rain in several southern districts. The weather system is expected to affect Odisha through September 26, raising the risk of flash floods, landslides and falling rocks, particularly in hilly areas. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall in Koraput, Nabarangpur, Rayagada, Ganjam, Gajapati, Kalahandi and Malkangiri, with adjoining districts also likely to receive heavy showers. Several parts of southern and coastal Odisha have already reported heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over the past 24 hours. Fallen trees have blocked roads, while landslides have disrupted connectivity in parts of Ganjam and Gajapati. Water levels have also risen in the Rushikulya, Bada Nadi and Loharakhandi rivers. In Ganjam, a landslide near Chariabada village in Patrapur block disrupted road connectivity. Another landslide was reported on the road leading to the Taratarini temple. A bridge on a rural road in Manipur village under Dharakote block was also damaged. In Gajapati, a landslide near Pariveta village in R. Udayagiri block affected connectivity to Bastriguda panchayat and Nuagada block. Heavy rain damaged houses in several panchayats in Koraput, while some trains were cancelled. Rising water levels in the Upper Kolab reservoir have added to concerns, with one gate of the Telingiri dam opened after the water level approached the danger mark. Separately, a wall collapse in Remuna block of Balasore district claimed one life and left his son seriously injured. The deep depression crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kalingapatnam, between Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, on Wednesday night. It brought heavy rain and winds of around 55–65 kmph to parts of Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. The system is expected to enter Odisha through Koraput on Thursday and gradually weaken. It may move through Narayanpatna, Laxmipur and Pottangi in Koraput before affecting parts of Rayagada, Nabarangpur and Kalahandi and then moving towards Chhattisgarh. The IMD has forecast isolated rainfall exceeding 200 mm in Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri. Winds of 50–60 kmph are also possible over southern Odisha. Odisha rain forecast for Thursday, Friday On Thursday, most parts of Odisha are likely to receive rainfall. Extremely heavy rain is possible in Nabarangpur, while Bargarh, Nuapada, Balangir, Kalahandi, Koraput and Malkangiri may receive heavy to very heavy showers. On Friday, extremely heavy rainfall is likely in Nuapada, Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri. Neighbouring districts are also expected to receive heavy rain, with winds potentially reaching 30–50 kmph. Andhra Pradesh power utilities on high alert In Andhra Pradesh, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar on Wednesday directed power utilities to remain on round-the-clock high alert amid the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal. Kumar reviewed the preparedness and operational status of the state's power sector, including weather conditions, electricity supply and response measures. "Kumar directed APTRANSCO and all DISCOMs to remain on high alert round the clock and take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted power supply across the state," a press release said. He asked officials to mobilise restoration teams wherever required and restore electricity at the earliest in case of localised disruptions. The minister also directed officials to monitor feeder-wise breakdowns, restoration work and load conditions through corporate monitoring centres and provide regular updates until normal operations resume. Kumar further directed Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation Limited officials to maintain adequate coal stocks at thermal power plants to ensure uninterrupted power generation. Hyderabad, Sept. 24 (Maxim News): AP Telangana Weather remains under close watch as heavy rains lash several districts after a deep depression crossed the North Andhra coast. The India Meteorological Department has warned of extremely heavy rain in Telangana on Thursday and Friday.

The deep depression moved inland after crossing the North Andhra coast near Kalingapatnam. The system had moved northwest at about 5 kmph during the six hours before the latest IMD bulletin. It lay near the North Andhra coast on Wednesday evening.
However, the weather system continues to influence rainfall across the region. Coastal Andhra Pradesh faces further heavy rain on Thursday. The IMD has also forecast strong winds and thunderstorms in parts of the state.

Meanwhile, Telangana faces a fresh spell of intense rainfall. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rain in the state on September 24 and September 25. It expects heavy rain on September 26. The department currently shows no warning for Telangana from September 27.
AP Telangana Weather alert continues as officials step up monitoring
The latest AP Telangana Weather outlook has prompted authorities to maintain close ground level monitoring. Officials have warned residents in vulnerable areas about possible flooding, waterlogging and strong winds.

In Telangana, districts in the northern and eastern parts face the strongest rainfall threat. The warning covers areas including Komuram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Mulugu and Bhadradri Kothagudem.
The weather system may also cause intense rainfall in adjoining districts. Therefore, residents should follow local administration advisories during periods of heavy rain.

In Andhra Pradesh, North Coastal Andhra has faced the strongest impact. Heavy rainfall has affected several areas since Wednesday. Reports also indicate substantial rainfall in and around Visakhapatnam.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has kept response teams ready in vulnerable districts. Officials have also monitored low lying areas and prepared rescue arrangements.

Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu also held a teleconference with collectors of rain affected districts on Thursday. He directed officials to remain alert as rain may continue through Thursday and Friday.
Naidu asked collectors to monitor water flows and vulnerable areas. He also directed them to take preventive measures around tanks and reservoirs. Furthermore, he stressed quick action whenever field teams request assistance.

The Chief Minister also stressed uninterrupted essential services. Officials must ensure power, drinking water and other basic services remain available in affected areas. He also asked authorities to maintain control rooms and gather field level information.
The administration has also focused on the risk of sudden flooding. Low lying areas can face rapid water accumulation after intense rainfall. Therefore, residents should avoid crossing overflowing streams and flooded roads.

The IMD expects the strongest rainfall threat in Telangana through Friday. Conditions should gradually improve after the current warning period.

articles.full_text:
Rainfall continued across Odisha on Thursday as the state came under the influence of the Deep Depression that crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early on September 24.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rainfall warnings for several districts, with heavy rain expected across southern, western and northern parts of Odisha.
Nabarangapur has been placed under a Red Warning for the possibility of extremely heavy rainfall.
Six districts — Bargarh, Nuapada, Balangir, Kalahandi, Koraput and Malkangiri — are under an Orange Warning for the likelihood of heavy to very heavy rainfall.
A Yellow Warning has also been issued for nine districts — Balasore, Sambalpur, Jharsuguda, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Subarnapur, Boudh, Kandhamal and Rayagada — indicating the possibility of heavy rain.
Deep Depression Crosses Andhra Coast
The Deep Depression crossed the coast near southwest of Kalingapatnam between 11 pm on September 23 and 1 am on September 24, according to the latest IMD bulletin.
The system crossed the coast with maximum sustained winds of 55-65 kmph, gusting up to 75 kmph, before moving west-northwestwards over north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
At 5.30 am on Thursday, the system lay centred over north coastal Andhra Pradesh, about 50 km west of Kalingapatnam, 80 km north-northeast of Visakhapatnam and 170 km southwest of Gopalpur in Odisha.
The system is expected to move northwestwards initially while maintaining its intensity as a Deep Depression for around 12 hours before moving north-northwestwards and gradually weakening.
Heavy Rain Likely Across Odisha
Under the system’s influence, heavy rainfall has continued in southern Odisha, while intermittent showers have been reported from several parts of coastal and western Odisha.
The weather department has forecast rainfall over most parts of the state on Thursday, with particularly intense spells likely in southern and western districts.
The latest warnings have placed Nabarangapur under the highest alert level, while residents in the six Orange Warning districts have been advised to remain cautious as heavy to very heavy rainfall could affect normal life.
